title: Extcap: Extcaps must be fully configured before start of capture
description:
When capture is started from the toolbar menu, no checks of extcap setting are
made.

Patch adds check of all selected extcaps before start of capture. If
extcap is not configured, extcap config dialog is shown for every
unconfigured extcap. Start of capture is canceled and a user must start
it again.

Changes:
- added check to MainWindow::startCapture()
- extcap options dialog shows Save or Start button, calling adapted

Fixes #13663

notes.body:
All calling sides are in #ifdef HAVE_LIBPCAP so I decided to use it there too. Now I found that welcome_page is the only exception - but it is mistake from my point of view.

Should I remove it in header file or should I guard welcome_page too to make it consistent?
I'm not sure I got the point, but HAVE_LIBPCAP guards code that should not be compiled if libpcap is not linked. Extcaps don't depend on it.

Extcaps do not depend on LIBPCAP, but capture start in MainWindow::startCapture() is guarded with #define HAVE_LIBPCAP. So I'm not sure whether there is any other way how to start extcap capture without pcap.

Should I test it?
I guess so. As far as I know, having extcaps without having libpcap is one of the most interesting scenarios. It should be fully supported, if it is not.

Extcap is the present, that keeps on giving ;-)

So, back in the day, libpcap was needed as it was the library used to decipher the pcap stream between dumpcap and Wireshark. You don't really need it for actual capture, but for reading what that capture program is sending. If this is still the case, I cannot say, but this is the main reason for having the #ifdef in the. first place. But yes, I must say it should be possible to capture with extcap only, if the library is no longer required for simply reading the stream.

Keep in mind, that the original extcap implementation started in 2014, my code parts where integrated in 2016. A lot decisions may seem outdated from todays perspective

I compiled WS without pcap support and it offers no interfaces - physical nor extcaps even extcaps are compiled. But as I see the code, it is because #ifdef HAVE_LIBPCAP in many places.

Extcaps (all I know) are sending data with libpcap_write_packet() which do not require libpcap, but on receiver side is dumpcap mentioned by Roland. So it looks to me that compiling without PCAP should disable all extcap related stuff too.

So I think that my #ifdef is OK except it should be added to welcome_page too.

Do you agree?
